intro.speaker: sam
intro.text: Hi! I'm new to this paper and my notes are a mess. Can you check them with me as we go?

L1U1.speaker: sam
L1U1.text: So… testing yourself is just better, always? Let's see what the study actually says.

L1U2.speaker: sam
L1U2.text: I filed highlighting under 'active studying'. Was that right?

L1U3.speaker: sam
L1U3.text: My friend has a test next week. What should she do on the metro?

item.speaker: sam
item.prompt: Sam's notes. One line is wrong — show Sam the passage that proves it.

statements.text: Recall group: remembered clearly more after one week.

sourceRefs.quote: One week later the recall group remembered clearly more.

statements.text: Highlighting is retrieval practice because you're being active.
statements.why: Highlighting puts the text in front of you again — it is re-exposure, not recall.

sourceRefs.quote: Re-reading, highlighting and reviewing a summary put the information in front of you again without asking you to recall it.

statements.text: Transfer to new problems: not tested.

sourceRefs.quote: Whether it transfers to new problems was not tested in this study.

hints: Does highlighting make you pull anything out of memory?

outro.speaker: sam
outro.text: Thanks! I'll fix my notes. Explaining it to me was probably the best revision you did today.
